html:
Latte stones are stone pillars topped with half-round capstones that held up the houses of the Chamorro people of Guam and the Mariana Islands. They were built from around 900 CE until Spanish conquest.

Pairs of pillars, some taller than a person, stood in rows under houses of chiefs and families. The largest, at the House of Taga on Tinian, were over 5 metres high. The dead were often buried beneath them.

After the Spanish-Chamorro Wars the villages that built them were abandoned. The latte is now the emblem of Chamorro identity and appears on the flag of the Northern Mariana Islands. See the first settlement of the Marianas and Nan Madol.
sum: Latte stones are stone pillars topped with half-round capstones that held up the houses of the Chamorro people of Guam and the Mariana Islands. They were built from around 900 CE until Spanish conquest.
